summary.title: FIPO: Eliciting Deep Reasoning with Future-KL Influenced Policy Optimization

details: GRPO-style RLVR with outcome-only rewards broadcasts one scalar advantage uniformly over all tokens, giving coarse credit assignment that caps reasoning depth (response length plateaus) unless one reverts to a critic/value model as in PPO.
Goal: obtain dense, token-level credit assignment inside the critic-free GRPO framework.
FIPO: a GRPO/DAPO-style policy objective in which each token's group-relative advantage is multiplied by an influence weight f_t = clip(exp(FutureKL_t), 1-eps_low, 1+eps_high).

FutureKL_t is the discounted (gamma^(k-t), gamma = 2^(-1/tau)) sum of signed log-probability shifts Δlog p_k = log π_θ − log π_old over the token's future trajectory, i.e. a forward-looking measure of whether the update reinforces or suppresses the continuation initiated by that token.
Stability mechanisms intrinsic to the method: masking tokens whose importance ratio exceeds the dual-clip threshold out of the FutureKL sum, and clipping the resulting influence weight.
Main experiments on Qwen2.5-32B-Base (a clean base model with no long-CoT SFT/distillation); pilot/ablations on Qwen2.5-7B-Math.
Trained on the publicly released DAPO-17K math dataset only, for a strictly controlled comparison.
Built on the verl framework and DAPO codebase; code and recipes open-sourced.

Global batch 512 prompts x G=16 rollouts; mini-batch enlarged from 32 to 64 prompts (8 gradient updates/iteration) for stability; lr 1e-6, weight decay 0.1, asymmetric policy clip [0.2, 0.28], no KL penalty, dual-clip ratio 10.
Max response length 20,480 with overlong penalty beyond 16,384.

FIPO-specific: decay horizon tau=32, influence-weight clip [1.0, 1.2] for 32B ([0.8, 1.2] for 7B), safety threshold 10 (3 for 7B); f_t reset to 1 for negative-advantage tokens with extreme importance ratios.
Chunked O(B·L + L·K)-memory implementation of the O(L^2) FutureKL aggregation.
AIME 2024 (primary) and AIME 2025; Pass@1 averaged over 32 samples, plus Cons@32 and Pass@32; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.7.
Baselines: reproduced DAPO (primary), GRPO (7B), and reported numbers for DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Math-32B and o1-mini.
Extreme importance-ratio filtering in FutureKL on/off; influence-weight clip range [1.0,1.2] vs [0.8,1.2]; decay horizon tau in {8, 32, 128, 256}.
Response-length control: raising clip-high to 1.4 and extending max length to 25K.
Mini-batch size 32 vs 64, and removing the overlong penalty.

key_findings.finding: Re-weighting outcome-based advantages by discounted future-KL breaks the length/performance plateau of DAPO on a clean base model.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen2.5-32B-Base, average CoT length grows from DAPO's ~4,000-token plateau to over 10,000 tokens (median rising from ~200 to >10,000), and AIME 2024 Pass@1 (Avg@32) rises from 50.0% to 56.0% converged (58.0% peak), with AIME 2025 rising 38%→43%; this exceeds DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Math-32B (~47%) and matches/exceeds o1-mini (~56%).

key_findings.finding: Dense credit assignment is achievable without a critic, closing the gap to PPO-based recipes that rely on value models pre-trained on long-CoT SFT data.
key_findings.evidence: FIPO is a pure GRPO/DAPO modification with no value network and no long-CoT priors, yet reaches performance comparable or superior to PPO-family baselines (VC-PPO/VAPO/T-PPO line) and clearly above the critic-free Open-Reasoner-Zero/DAPO setting.

key_findings.finding: Unregulated future-KL accumulation is unstable, and masking dual-clip-triggering tokens plus clipping the influence weight is necessary.
key_findings.evidence: Vanilla FutureKL runs collapse around step 70 with a spike in low-clip fraction, surging Policy KL and gradient norm, and an abrupt drop in response length; on 7B, removing extreme-IS-ratio filtering widens the influence-weight range and raises dual-clip and policy-clip fractions, lowering AIME 2024 peak from 40.0% to 38.0%.

key_findings.finding: FIPO's gains come with healthier optimization dynamics and a self-reinforcing length-advantage loop, whereas DAPO shows signs of overfitting.
key_findings.evidence: FIPO shows steadily rising length-weighted mean advantage, smooth entropy growth, low stable gradient norms and structured Policy KL drift, while DAPO's weighted advantage declines, gradient norms spike volatilely, and its number of sampled batches escalates (more non-discriminative all-correct/all-wrong groups); accuracy correlates positively with length across all training phases.

key_findings.finding: Optimal exploration pressure is scale-dependent: 32B benefits from high-entropy exploration while 7B performs best converging to a low-entropy reasoning manifold.
key_findings.evidence: On 7B-Math, the [1.0,1.2] influence-weight clip that works best at 32B drives continuous entropy growth but only 36.0% AIME 2024, versus 40.0% with the balanced [0.8,1.2] range; tau=32 balances weight volatility against premature entropy collapse (tau=8) and excessive exploration (tau=256), and 7B response length stays flat around 1200 tokens rather than scaling.
